the capital region's edge is in dollars, not awards
40.8% of the 547,968 awards carrying both codes are performed outside the recipient's state, 36.1%
of the dollars, and every department does it — 33% at Agriculture to 54% at Energy, with NASA the
exception at 19%. DC, Maryland and Virginia are 19.4% of awards by address and 20.3% by
performance — barely different — but 31.7% and 29.3% of the dollars. Inside the region the two
measures point opposite ways: 80% of DC-performed awards go to an out-of-state recipient, and 54%
of Virginia's own awards are performed somewhere else.
place is durable, and it is not merely the agency mix
Agency mix is half of it: scored at national per-agency rates it spans 18 of the
32-point raw spread and accounts for 49% of the variance between states. The half it
leaves does not wash out. A state's FY2015 single-offer rate predicts its FY2017 rate at
r +0.72, and still at r +0.67 once each year's agency mix is removed — so the spread is
not agencies rotating through. The national rate barely moves (59.4%, 59.5%, 58.6%)
while the median state swings 4.1 points and MI moves 52% to 65%. Offer coverage is
99.8%, 99.7% and 98.7%, so the three years are comparable on this column.
USAspending API v2 bulk download, fetched 2026-09-22; FY2016, with FY2015 and FY2017 for the right panel. CAVEAT: both axes on the left are shares of the national award count and so track
population; only the departure from the diagonal is a within-state quantity. These eleven civilian departments are 8.5% of federal contract awards; Defense (68.6%) is absent, so this is not
